messages:
maya: Quick idea — add compatibility-aware alias resolution in the gateway so model alias -> version selection can enforce compatibility constraints (seq_len, quant, kv-cache shape) before promoting a variant. Trying to avoid client-side hacks.

anil: Can you sketch how clients would pick? header-driven (eg X-Model-Alias) or route config?

maya: Prefer route config. Client sends alias+hints (e.g., max_seq, prefer_quantized) and gateway chooses the best compatible pinned/rolled-out version. That keeps telemetry and quotas centralized.

jess: Draft config snippet (very rough):

```json
{
  "route_id": "chat.create",
  "alias_rules": [
    {
      "alias": "redwood-chat-medium",
      "candidates": [
        {"version": "rm-chat-m-1.2-qat", "constraints": {"quant": true, "max_seq": 2048}, "weight": 0.0},
        {"version": "rm-chat-m-1.3-fp16", "constraints": {"quant": false, "max_seq": 8192}, "weight": 1.0}
      ],
      "fallback": "nearest_compatible"
    }
  ]
}
```

jess: Gateway would check each candidate in order of weight, verify constraints vs request (seq_len, quant preference, kv shape), and pick first compatible.

nick: Two concerns: 1) If a pinned version is incompatible we must not silently pick a heavier variant and blow the customer's quota/cost. 2) Need deterministic fallback ordering so tests are stable.

sara: For quotas: if fallback picks a larger model, telemetry should attach an "effective_model_cost" tag and we should consult route-level budget. If over budget, either deny or fall back to a cheaper degraded model (e.g., shorter max_tokens) and return a structured 4xx with reason.

manil: @sara +1 — also need an explicit opt-out header for clients that refuse degraded/expensive fallbacks: `X-Allow-Fallback: false`.

maya: Good call. Thinking to expose a 3-way decision: PICKED, FALLBACK (why), DENIED (quota/compat). And add telemetry labels: ["route_id","alias","picked_version","picked_reason","request_seq","request_quant_pref","effective_cost_units"].

jess: UX -> console: we should show compatibility matrix per alias (versions vs constraints) and warn when doing canary rollouts that some customer traffic will be routed to incompatible variants. Also provide a preview simulation button that runs a sample request through routing logic.

nick: Implementation note: runtime needs fast constraint checks (avoid deserializing full model metadata per request). We should cache per-model capability tuples (max_seq, quant_modes, kv_layout) in routing layer and invalidate on model onboard events.

ops-bot: integration-test /alias-routing: failing 3/120 — edge-case where `nearest_compatible` picked fp16 variant but request had quant-only session.

jess: ops-bot — can you paste failing request logs?

ops-bot: 
```
request: {"alias":"redwood-chat-medium","seq_len":1024,"prefer_quant":true}
candidates checked: [rm-chat-m-1.2-qat, rm-chat-m-1.3-fp16]
selected: rm-chat-m-1.3-fp16
reason: caching stale capabilities: rm-chat-m-1.2 reported quant:true but registry has removed quant build
```

nick: Sounds like a cache invalidation bug. We should tag cached entries with model_registry_version and check on change.

anil: Policy question: should route config allow a strict-pin mode (refuse any fallback) vs flexible mode? This impacts rollout UX: strict-pin useful for regulated customers.

maya: I propose defaults: flexible mode for PLG routes, strict-pin opt-in per route for enterprise. Console toggle, API field `pin_mode: [flexible|strict]`.

sara: Also require explicit acceptance for auto-cost-increase in flexible mode. Add `allow_cost_increase_percent` with default 0.

jess: For telemetry/observability: add per-request annotation `routing_decision` with values PICKED/FALLBACK/DENIED and `decision_reason` free text (compat, quota, pin). Hook these to per-route dashboards and an alert when fallback_rate > 1%.

maya: Next steps: I'll open RFC with config schema + telemetry labels + console mockups. @nick + @jess to take runtime cache invalidation + fast capability check. @sara please write quota interaction cases.

anil: +1. one small nit: let's prefer header `X-Model-Alias` only as override; route config wins. Document precedence.

deploy-bot: Staging deploy scheduled: alias-routing-v2 -> canary (5%) at 2026-04-02T02:00Z :rocket:

jess: :+1: will add canary telemetry to track "incompatible-fallback" events during rollout.

maya: Thanks all — RFC link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/559 (WIP).
